analysis.title: GS Sector Specialists Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview: Tuesday Thoughts, 2 Prints (3 Nov 2026)
key_insights: MPC: Marathon Petroleum is divesting its Minnesota and North Dakota refineries and MPLX is divesting related midstream assets. The asset sales are expected to be the focus of the 11 AM ET call, more than the quarter itself.

MPC 3Q EPS is about 4% above Street numbers. Refining has seen double-digit EPS beats throughout this earnings season, and most of those prints were faded. The desk thinks the buyside was closer to a 3 handle on EPS.

MPC capture rate of 93% was well telegraphed and in line with the historic average for 3Q results. The company repurchased $3 bn of shares in the quarter, and early call questions are expected on whether the shareholder returns strategy shifts.
MPC is sitting on +$12 of cash (unit as printed in the note, likely billions), against a target range closer to ~$1 bn over time.
MPC bar was high because the stock held up well against large-cap peers over the last month. With the asset sales and Refining reporting in later innings, the print is expected to matter less.

MPC asset sales total about 180 kbd of capacity for $3.45 bn net to MPC, with MPLX receiving $750 mn. The company is discussing investing in the Gulf Coast (possibly debottlenecking) and supporting MPLX growth.
MPLX portion of the deal is expected to draw heavy attention from both Refining and Midstream investors, specifically on where and whether inorganic growth fits the narrative.

SU: Suncor is one of the more well owned stocks in the US and the bar is high for the EPS print. Desk conversations point to strong beat expectations on Downstream, similar to 2Q when Downstream results were more in line with buyside expectations.

SU: Most investors have been watching SCO and the distillate chart over the last couple of months, showing a relative preference to still own the stock. Call questions are expected on core vs non-core assets and use of cash.

SU: CAD peers have signaled willingness to grow and there are several headlines on consolidation in Canada. The desk expects tight messaging: no real change to assets competing for capital, kits running at high utilization, cost take-out.
SU: Positioning is a concern for the print. With WCS (Western Canadian Select) still wide, the desk thinks most investors would rather hold names without heavy exposure to it.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q EPS about 4% above Street, but refining beats have been faded this season. The asset sale announcement and the call at 11 AM ET are the focus.
MPLX is divesting related midstream assets and receiving $750 mn. Investors will focus on where inorganic growth fits.
Stock is well owned and the EPS bar is high, with strong Downstream beat expectations already in place. Positioning is a risk into the print.

tension_points.bear_case: The 4% EPS beat is modest next to the double-digit beats seen in Refining this season, most of which were faded, and the stock held up well versus large-cap peers going in, so the bar was high.
